newsitem.title: PERU: Peru settles Russian debt, but terms unclear.
newsitem.headline: Peru settles Russian debt, but terms unclear.

text.p: Peru has settled its $1 billion debt with Russian creditors, following a restructuring agreement announced last year, said President Alberto Fujimori.
The two countries had disagreements on exactly how much Peru owed to Russian creditors but the final figure was set at about $1 billion, Fujimori said.
"Today some news has come out which has not been divulged. We have paid off the Russian debt," he said.

"To speak in overall figures, the Russian debt was approximately $1 billion, and we have negotiated (to settlle it) with less than $200 million," he said in an interview on Panamericana Television on Sunday night.
He gave no details on whether Peru would pay only the $200 million or whether more payments were scheduled for later.

Fujimori announced in the southern city of Arequipa last December that Peru and Russia agreed to restructure $162 million of debt. Disagreements on exchange rates and the size of the total debt had delayed completion of the deal, one of a series of recent debt pacts worked out by Peruvian negotiators.
The main agreement was a Brady deal signed exactly one month ago, restructuring $4.3 billion of the country's external debt with about 180 mainly North American creditors.
